title: Core lemma (infinite mean, n>=3): convergence of the matched truncation in E[X1 1_{A_t}] = mu P(A_t)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
This is the decisive gap. After symmetrizing the realizing vector by a uniform random permutation, (X1,...,Xn) may be taken exchangeable with each Xi ~ F and sum = n*mu a.s. For t>0 set A_t = {max_i |X_i| <= t}. On A_t all |X_i|<=t and sum = n*mu, so by exchangeability
   E[X1 1_{A_t}] = mu * P(A_t).   (star)
Since P(A_t) -> 1, (star) pins mu provided E[X1 1_{A_t}] converges. Writing the F-only truncated mean f(t) := E_F[X 1_{|X|<=t}],
   f(t) = E[X1 1_{A_t}] + R(t),   R(t) := E[X1 1_{|X1|<=t} 1_{A_t^c}],
so f(t) = mu*P(A_t) + R(t). The error R(t) depends on the JOINT coupling, NOT on F alone (it is the contribution of '|X1|<=t but some partner exceeds t').

WHAT MUST BE PROVED: that two different centers mu and nu (realized by DIFFERENT couplings of the same marginal F, on different probability spaces) must coincide. The natural route is to show that E[X1 1_{A_t}] converges to a quantity determined by F alone (a principal-value / matched truncated mean), independent of the coupling; then mu = nu. Equivalently show R(t) -> 0 or otherwise control f(t). For the counterexample of issue rm-02063-2, f(t) does converge to the center via cancellation of equal-order +/- tails (both ~ (2/3)C ln K with t ~ 2^K), but in general f(t) need not converge, and the truncation in A_t is by {|X_i|<=t for ALL i}, not by {|X1|<=t}. Resolving this rigorously is the heart of the problem.

Useful tools to try: A_t^c = union_{j} {|X_j|>t}; the forced-deficit inclusion {X1>t} subset union_{j>=2}{X_j < (n*mu - t)/(n-1)} giving P(|X1|>t) <= (n-1) P(|X1| > (t-|n*mu|)/(n-1)) to bound the tail mass entering R(t).
